description: Textile explores the fibers and fabrics around us: what textiles are, natural and synthetic fibers, how yarn and fabric are made, hands-on projects such as weaving, felting and dyeing, textile terms, environmental concerns, and careers.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: What textiles are
requirements.summary: Why textiles matter and what fiber, fabric and textile mean.

requirements.title: Fibers and fabrics
requirements.summary: Samples of natural, synthetic and cellulosic fabrics, and how fiber becomes yarn and fabric.

requirements.title: Textile projects
requirements.summary: Two options, such as weaving on a homemade loom, making felt, natural dyeing or testing fibers.

requirements.title: Textile terms
requirements.summary: Terms such as warp, heddle, loom and worsted.

requirements.title: Fibers and the environment
requirements.summary: Pros and cons of the main fiber types and environmental concerns in textile production.

requirements.title: Careers
requirements.summary: Careers in the textile industry and two that interest you.
